hypothesis: Storing the weights in S3 One Zone-IA instead of S3 Standard does not change weight-download time or init latency: One Zone-IA is a cheaper storage class with the same first-byte latency and throughput, not a performance tier. It adds a $0.01/GB retrieval fee on every cold start and snapshot init.

conclusion: No change (pre-registered rule). Cold weight_download p50: Standard 24.99 s, One Zone-IA 25.03 s; ratio 1.0016, bootstrap 95% CI [0.9978, 1.0054], inside the +/-2% band (n=50 each, 79 MiB/s both). On Graviton3 alone the ratio is 0.9995 [0.997, 1.005]. Snapshot-init download 0.9998 [0.995, 1.011]. Cold first request total 35.93 vs 35.95 s, Restore Duration 3.22 vs 3.21 s, warm inference 0.66 vs 0.66 s: every interval contains 1.0, apart from the cold probe forward on Graviton3, +1.9 ms (+0.8%), which runs on weights already in memory. 1,200 invocations, 0 errors, 0 class mismatches, 1,200/1,200 answers bit-identical to the P1 reference, and the same answer SHA-256 on both arms. Cost is the only effect. One Zone-IA charges $0.0208 per download ($20.80 per 1,000 cold starts or snapshot inits), against $0.000013 for Standard and $0.0012 at Express One Zone list prices. It saves $0.027 per month in storage on this 2.08 GB object, so it breaks even at 1.3 downloads per month and has a 30-day minimum. Restores read no S3 bytes. Recommendation: keep the weights in S3 Standard.

decision.statistic: ratio ozia/std of medians, bootstrap 95% interval (10,000 resamples, seed 0)
decision.rule: no-change if the interval lies inside the band; improved if its upper end is below 0.98; regressed if its lower end is above 1.02; otherwise inconclusive
